To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the health care of older persons in Singapore is a complex issue that needs to be addressed in the context of a rapidly ageing society.
the social policy in Singapore is a case of the state providing a wide range of services, but the individual and the community are left to make the choices and to manage the services.
the state of Singapore has been able to provide a wide range of services to the ageing population, but there is still room for improvement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the social and health care needs of older persons in Singapore?
the social policy of health care and the social policy of care in a context of ageing in Singapore.

the following: (1) the development of a conceptual framework for mapping out the health care system for older persons; (2) the identification of the gaps in the health care system; (3) the development of an integrated system of health care for older people; and (4) the development of health care social policy in a multicultural society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social policy of health care in Singapore has been successful in the sense that it has been able to provide essential health care to all Singaporeans.
the state is not doing enough for the older person in Singapore, and that there is a great deal of work to be done.
health care for older people is not an area of concern for the state in Singapore.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a need to re-orientate our social policy to the individual, to be more flexible and less bureaucratic, to provide more services and more subsidies to the individual/family to enable the individual to age in place, to be able to choose the services that he/she wants and to provide more support for the family to enable the family to care for the older member.
we have identified the need for a new paradigm for health care social policy for older persons in the light of changing demographic and social profiles.
we need to look at the individual as an integral part of the community and the state and not as a recipient of services.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a social policy should not only focus on the older person but on the family as a whole.
a health care system for the elderly must be based on a model of care that recognises the needs of the individual as well as those of the family.
the state should not only be concerned with the economic and health status of its older citizens, but also with the social and cultural well-being of its older citizens.
